implemented.label: Implemented
implemented.meaning: The runner or a maintained skill enforces it and records evidence.

conditional.label: Conditional
conditional.meaning: Enforced when the plan selects it.

partial.label: Partial
partial.meaning: Addresses part of the checkpoint; a material gap remains.

external.label: External
external.meaning: Belongs to source control, identity, or organizational operations. External is not a pass.

gap.label: Gap
gap.meaning: Not provided by the current execution environment.

policy.label: Policy choice
policy.meaning: A deliberate design choice that differs from the checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Spec has a start locus and a completion artifact
checkpoints.how: `specify` writes four plan files plus `pipeline.json`. Validation rejects a plan unless every outcome maps to an existing check with a green phase.
checkpoints.remains: Plan quality still depends on your confirmation.

checkpoints.title: Ambiguity surfaced before the first write
checkpoints.how: `specify` reads instructions and nearby examples first, then asks only for genuinely missing decisions before anything starts.
checkpoints.remains: Nothing within the workflow boundary.

checkpoints.title: Task prioritized before assignment
checkpoints.how: Tracker connectors and the GitHub adapter can read an issue.
checkpoints.remains: Priority and ownership belong to your tracker and team process.

checkpoints.title: Task size bounded
checkpoints.how: Declared writable path patterns bound what a task may change, per repository.
checkpoints.remains: There is no line or file budget, and no split suggestion for a large diff.

checkpoints.title: Agent instruction file at the repository root, in version control
checkpoints.how: Setup writes `PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md` and a managed block in each repository's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, preserving your prose.
checkpoints.remains: In a non-Git parent folder, `PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md` is versioned only if you choose a configuration repository.

checkpoints.title: Instruction file pruned, not just grown
checkpoints.how: `prune-context` proposes evidence-based removals and relocations; rules stay scoped instead of bloating root guidance.
checkpoints.remains: It works from examples you supply and is proposal-only. Nothing collects evidence or schedules a pruning pass.

checkpoints.title: Environment declarative and snapshotted
checkpoints.how: Commands and test environments are declared in the profile. Each run snapshots the effective profile, skills, rules, and references.
checkpoints.remains: Agent stages use the host environment, not an immutable environment image.

checkpoints.title: Docs and architecture layers machine-checked
checkpoints.how: Blocking rules can run any deterministic command or forbidden-pattern detector against changed files.
checkpoints.remains: Documentation cross-links and layer checks belong in your repository's CI.

checkpoints.title: Agent discoveries captured as skills and scripts
checkpoints.how: `add-rule`, `rule record`, `skill new`, skill overrides, and custom stages turn repeated discoveries into project-owned controls.
checkpoints.remains: Someone still has to choose to capture them.

checkpoints.title: Read-only explore phase before execution
checkpoints.how: `specify` researches instructions and working examples before it proposes anything, and records the result as plan files.
checkpoints.remains: The explore phase is a skill instruction, not a mechanically read-only sandbox.

checkpoints.title: Plan reviewed by a non-author
checkpoints.how: You review and confirm the complete plan. `validate-plan` and `preflight` check it mechanically before any stage runs.
checkpoints.remains: A second automated plan critic is not a default stage.

checkpoints.title: Planning and implementation contexts separated
checkpoints.how: Stages start fresh sessions from the plan files. A plan revision changes the binding hash; `resume --rebind` archives the old inputs and invalidates affected stages.
checkpoints.remains: Nothing within the workflow boundary.

checkpoints.title: Vertical slices, each independently testable
checkpoints.how: Every outcome maps to named executable checks.
checkpoints.remains: The runner does not prove that a plan is a vertical slice.

checkpoints.title: Unattended runs inside an isolation boundary
checkpoints.how: Restricted mode uses provider controls: the Codex workspace-write sandbox, the Cursor sandbox, or an explicit Claude tool allowlist. Every stage is followed by path and evidence guards.
checkpoints.remains: Trusted mode, the offered default, is not operating-system containment.

checkpoints.title: Network egress allowlisted
checkpoints.how: The runner does not control network access.
checkpoints.remains: Provider, package, source-control, and general egress need an environment-level firewall.

checkpoints.title: Untrusted content sanitized before the model
checkpoints.how: Every stage prompt says external files, issue text, logs, and tool results are evidence, never instructions. `specify` and `address-pr-comments` repeat it for fetched text.
checkpoints.remains: This is instruction-level. There is no deterministic sanitizer.

checkpoints.title: Risk tiers gate what runs automatically
checkpoints.how: The permission mode, path scope, blocking guards, and a separate authorization for every external action decide what runs unattended.
checkpoints.remains: There is no risk classification that changes behavior by itself.

checkpoints.title: Parallel agents in isolated checkouts
checkpoints.how: The worktree strategy isolates task checkouts. One runner per project is deliberate, held by an operating-system lock.
checkpoints.remains: Parallel runs relocate the review queue rather than shortening it; see Review and everyday use.

checkpoints.title: Agent-runnable check per task
checkpoints.how: Every outcome names checks with argv, working directory, parser, and timeout.
checkpoints.remains: The plan author must choose meaningful checks.

checkpoints.title: Completion gated deterministically
checkpoints.how: The runner executes the checks itself, parses their output, guards paths, rules, and frozen tests, and binds green evidence to a diff fingerprint.
checkpoints.remains: Nothing within the workflow boundary.

checkpoints.title: Fresh-context reviewer on the diff
checkpoints.how: The optional review stage starts fresh with the requirements and the actual diff, and never receives `implementation.md`.
checkpoints.remains: Review runs only when the plan selects it.

checkpoints.title: Behavioral verification for user-facing changes
checkpoints.how: Disposable environments with readiness patterns and leases, E2E skills, and `test-on-staging` cover behavior when the plan selects them.
checkpoints.remains: Screenshots and recordings are not required.

checkpoints.title: Agent-written tests reviewed adversarially
checkpoints.how: Tests are written first, must fail on an assertion rather than a setup error, and are frozen by hash for later stages.
checkpoints.remains: Mutation testing is not provided.

checkpoints.title: SAST, secret, and dependency scans before review
checkpoints.how: A built-in secret detector and your blocking rules run on every changed file, and again before publication.
checkpoints.remains: No SAST or dependency analysis is supplied.

checkpoints.title: Named human approver, no self-merge
checkpoints.how: The runner opens draft PRs only. It never approves or merges them; `merge-to-base` is a local, opt-in, user-requested skill.
checkpoints.remains: Branch protection and named approvers are configured in source control.

checkpoints.title: PR carries evidence, not assertions
checkpoints.how: Commands, parsed results, rules, and the diff fingerprint are recorded per stage. `pr-preflight` flags unsupported testing claims in a PR body.
checkpoints.remains: The draft PR body is the approved body file; evidence is not attached automatically.

checkpoints.title: Review capacity tracked as a constraint
checkpoints.how: Each task produces the evidence a reviewer needs.
checkpoints.remains: Review latency and queue size are organizational metrics.

checkpoints.title: Auto-fix loops bounded
checkpoints.how: Attempts per route (at most 5), run, inactivity, and tool timeouts, and bot polling (at most 10 rounds) are all bounded.
checkpoints.remains: Review the limits as usage changes.

checkpoints.title: Agent authorship labeled
checkpoints.how: Commit skills deliberately forbid AI attribution trailers.
checkpoints.remains: Provenance reporting needs a separate mechanism if you want it.

checkpoints.title: Sessions instrumented end to end
checkpoints.how: Each run keeps a journal, per-attempt records, evidence files, and provider usage when it is reported.
checkpoints.remains: There is no central telemetry export.

checkpoints.title: Failures feed back into instructions
checkpoints.how: `rule record` counts recurring examples and proposes a corrective review at the rule's `review_after` threshold.
checkpoints.remains: No unattended loop analyzes sessions or edits instructions.

checkpoints.title: Stability metrics segmented by provenance
checkpoints.how: Task evidence stays local to the project.
checkpoints.remains: Stability and rework dashboards belong to your organization.

checkpoints.title: Spend monitored, not incentivized
checkpoints.how: Usage and cost are recorded when the provider reports them; a missing cost stays unknown, never zero. Claude runs accept `max_budget_usd`.
checkpoints.remains: No central per-task spend reporting.

checkpoints.title: Agent credentials scoped and audited
checkpoints.how: Credentials come only from host logins or named `env_refs`; literal secrets in commands and connector settings are rejected.
checkpoints.remains: Credentials are inherited from the host, not issued per stage or short-lived.

checkpoints.title: Production access gated in multiple layers
checkpoints.how: `test-on-staging` defaults to non-destructive reads and needs explicit authorization for mutations.
checkpoints.remains: Identity, database, network, and audit layers are yours to provide.

checkpoints.title: Skills inventoried and evaluated
checkpoints.how: `skill list` and `skill resolve` show effective sources; skill metadata is validated; updates report changed upstream skills.
checkpoints.remains: There are no behavioral evaluations of skills.

beyond_rubric.title: Plan binding and rebind
beyond_rubric.why: Evidence belongs to one plan revision. A changed plan, profile, or skill stops the run until a reviewed `resume --rebind` archives the old inputs and invalidates affected stages.

beyond_rubric.title: Diff fingerprint
beyond_rubric.why: Green evidence is bound to a hash of the files. Any later change makes it stale, and delivery re-runs the checks.

beyond_rubric.title: Frozen tests
beyond_rubric.why: After red proof, test-file hashes are recorded. Implementation and review cannot rewrite, add, or delete those tests to get green.

beyond_rubric.title: Assertion-level red
beyond_rubric.why: Import, syntax, compile, and startup failures are rejected as red evidence; expected test identities must fail on assertions.

beyond_rubric.title: No silent skips
beyond_rubric.why: Skipped or pending tests fail a check unless the plan records a justification.

beyond_rubric.title: No implicit fallback
beyond_rubric.why: Only the ordered routes you approved are tried, and only for authentication, quota, or model failures.

beyond_rubric.title: Exact-session answers
beyond_rubric.why: An answer resumes the provider session that asked. It is never rerouted to another session or model.

beyond_rubric.title: Fresh sessions
beyond_rubric.why: Every stage and every retry starts a new session, so no chat history carries over.

beyond_rubric.title: Review without the reasoning
beyond_rubric.why: The review stage never receives `implementation.md`; it sees requirements and the actual diff.

beyond_rubric.title: Partial work preserved
beyond_rubric.why: A scope violation fails the run but keeps the changes for inspection. Nothing is reset or committed automatically.

beyond_rubric.title: Checks may not edit source
beyond_rubric.why: A verification command that changes repository files invalidates its own evidence.

beyond_rubric.title: Your changes stay yours
beyond_rubric.why: Pre-existing uncommitted changes are recorded at start. A stage that touches them fails, and delivery never commits them.

beyond_rubric.title: Approval-digest setup
beyond_rubric.why: Setup and connector patches apply only with the digest of the exact proposal you reviewed. A stale proposal is rejected.

beyond_rubric.title: Configuration snapshotted per run
beyond_rubric.why: Each run freezes the effective profile, skills, rules, and references, so a mid-run edit cannot change a stage's instructions.

beyond_rubric.title: One runner per project
beyond_rubric.why: An operating-system lock admits one runner per project. Cancellation asks the owner to stop its own process group and never kills a stale PID.

beyond_rubric.title: Guarded multi-repository delivery
beyond_rubric.why: Commits stage only task-owned paths, never base branches, never force-push, and resume per repository after a partial failure.

beyond_rubric.title: Read-only companion repositories
beyond_rubric.why: A repository can supply checks without getting a branch; any change to it is a scope violation.

beyond_rubric.title: Redacted questions and output
beyond_rubric.why: Tokens and keys are redacted from saved questions, errors, and command output.

beyond_rubric.title: Unknown cost stays unknown
beyond_rubric.why: Usage and cost appear only when the provider reports them. A missing cost is never shown as zero.

frontier.title: Operating-system isolation
frontier.detail: Run trusted stages inside a container or VM boundary instead of relying on provider flags and post-stage guards.

frontier.title: Network egress control
frontier.detail: Allowlist provider, package, and source-control hosts per stage.

frontier.title: Scoped credentials
frontier.detail: Issue short-lived, stage-scoped credentials instead of inheriting host logins.

frontier.title: Evidence in the pull request
frontier.detail: Attach the recorded check summary and fingerprint to the draft PR body.

frontier.title: Telemetry and organization metrics
frontier.detail: Export run journals, usage, and outcomes to a privacy-preserving central store.

frontier.title: Deterministic untrusted-input handling
frontier.detail: Wrap and flag fetched text in code rather than only by instruction.

frontier.title: Size and slicing signals
frontier.detail: Record diff size against a plan budget and suggest splits.

frontier.title: Skill evaluations
frontier.detail: Behavioral evals for the most-used skills.
